$comment: Declaration for scripts/verify/promotion-drift.sh — edit THIS, never the
script's internals, so there is exactly one place a number lives.
WHY THIS EXISTS. The 2026-09-10 dev-trunk directive made `dev` the
integration trunk: lane work lands there continuously because reaching it
costs no CI (every push trigger is branches:[main] or tags-only — verified
by the runs API, delta 0). That removes the deferral that stranded 33 of 33
branches on a sibling repo. But it RELOCATES the risk rather than removing
it: work in dev but not main stops reading as 'unlanded', so the dev->main
gap becomes invisible to the tooling that used to surface it.
The directive's own words: 'Without a standing promotion cadence, main rots
and the first promotion after a long gap is a large, hard-to-review merge —
the same bottleneck in a new place.' This gate is that cadence, made
$why_age: AGE is one of TWO triggers; promote when EITHER fires, whichever is first.
Ten landings in a day is a healthy trunk; ten over six weeks is rot, and a
count-only threshold cannot tell those apart. This measures the OLDEST
unpromoted commit, so a steady rhythm keeps it near zero however much lands.
REVISED 2026-09-10 from 14 to 3 days. The 14 was reasoned and UNMEASURED —
picked as 'two missed weekly promotions'. aegis measured the thing the
number is supposed to bound and it is not review size, it is PRODUCTION
DIVERGENCE: merging is gated by a required check, deploying is gated by
nothing, so the two drift apart silently. Their finding, from the same
trunk model: 72 hours, because elapsed time is what that pressure scales
with. Time is the only axis here that is actively unsafe rather than merely
expensive, so it gets the tighter bound.
section 4 (read on branch dev; identical blob on chore/ref-expiry 92afacf37).
$why_landings: The volume axis, and it counts INDEPENDENT LANDINGS (--first-parent), not
raw commits. That distinction is the correction, not a detail.
REVISED 2026-09-10 from 250 raw commits to 10 landings. The 250 mirrored
release-drift's threshold, which measures a DIFFERENT gap (main past the
last tag) where raw commits are the right unit. Here the pressure is
debug-on-red: a failed promotion tells you nothing about WHICH change broke
it, and that cost scales with the number of independent changes in the
batch, not with how many commits each one carried.
Measured on csq 2026-09-10: origin/main..origin/dev was 13 raw commits but
9 first-parent landings — the raw figure overstates the batch by 1.44x.
aegis measured 2.8x on their repo (250 raw = 89 landings). Different
magnitude, same direction, and reporting raw pushes toward promoting LESS
10 landings is about two days at aegis's measured steady state of ~5
independent changes/day. It is the trigger a burst day hits, which turns
one unreviewable promotion into several small ones.
$immediate_lane: Not a threshold — a bypass. Any security fix, deploy-affecting change, or
anything a deploy-drift check flags promotes IMMEDIATELY and does not wait
for a batch to fill. Risk should decide these, never volume. This gate
cannot detect that class, so it is stated here for the operator rather than

$amendment_2026_09_11: THE PREMISE ABOVE IS NO LONGER TRUE. Recorded, not acted on: the date is
deliberately left at 2026-10-08, because this block's own last paragraph
says moving it needs a dated rationale, and that warning applies with equal
force to moving it EARLIER. Pulling it in would make the gate stricter
sooner, which is the safe direction — but it is still the maintainer's call,
not a correction an agent makes while fixing a factual error.
What was measured on 2026-09-10/11, against the claim that
`Rust tests (windows-latest)` cannot obtain a runner:
- FOUR successful windows-latest runs that day (34482316755, 34485149432,
- The one that failed ran for SEVEN MINUTES (17:09:20Z to 17:16:20Z) and
failed on a real test, not on runner starvation: 3726 passed, 1 failed.
The claimed symptom was '2-3s, no runner, zero steps'. That is not what
the runs look like.
- The Actions spending caps were lifted by the maintainer, which is the
condition the original rationale was waiting on.
And the stronger disproof: promotion did not merely become POSSIBLE, it
HAPPENED. an internal ticket merged dev->main with 17/17 required contexts green,
including `Rust tests (windows-latest)` at 10m14s. A claim that promotion is
IMPOSSIBLE cannot survive a completed promotion.
So the 2026-10-08 date no longer rests on its stated reason. Its original
derivation — one week past the 2026-10-01 billing reset, giving one cadence
cycle after promotion becomes possible — is moot, because promotion became
possible three weeks early. The date is now merely CONSERVATIVE rather than
necessary, and a maintainer may pull it in at any time.
Left as a live decision rather than silently corrected, because a stale
premise and a wrong date are different defects: the first is a factual error
in a durable artifact (verify-claims-before-write.md MUST-1), the second is a
judgment about when a gate should start failing rather than warning.
